dedupe_keys.name: usda grain transportation report weekly grain transport volumes and prices

description: The Grain Transportation Report is a weekly publication and data set on how US grain moves to domestic and export markets by rail, barge, truck and ocean vessel. The US Department of Agriculture's Agricultural Marketing Service produces it to inform farmers, shippers and policy makers about transport conditions. Each issue reports the latest volumes and prices: rail car loadings and secondary railcar market bids, barge movements and freight rates on the Mississippi, Illinois and Ohio rivers with lock tonnages, truck rates, Great Lakes and ocean freight rates, export inspections by port region and grain inventories at ports, together with commentary on disruptions such as low water, lock closures, strikes and weather. The weekly issues and the underlying tables are free to download, with data sets available through the USDA open data platform, and AMS also publishes related quarterly reports on refrigerated truck transport. Caveats: the report is a national market summary, not shipment-level data, series definitions have changed over the years, and some rates come from industry sources that are not fully documented. Simulation uses: parameterising grain and food freight flows in supply chain network models, measuring how river low water or lock outages change costs and routes, and validating disruption scenarios for food supply resilience. Related records: USDA FGIS export grain inspections (data-usda-fgis-export-grain-inspections) give lot-level export volumes, and USDA PSD Online (data-usda-psd-online) supplies supply and demand balances.
